subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: Should OpenClaw accept this custom glob implementation and bootstrap-handler yielding as the permanent runtime fix for the reported event-loop stalls?
rationale: The implementation is technically well-supported, but CI cannot decide whether the residual glob-compatibility risk, changed session interleaving, and increased traversal wall time are acceptable product-runtime tradeoffs.

options.title: Accept after green checks
options.body: Approve the runtime tradeoffs, retain the parity and performance coverage, and merge once every required exact-head check passes.

options.title: Narrow the scheduling scope
options.body: Request a smaller revision that keeps asynchronous file loading and cooperative traversal but defers hook-handler scheduling changes to separate runtime work.

options.title: Pause the custom walker
options.body: Hold the PR until maintainers prefer a dependency or architectural approach that avoids owning native-glob compatibility in core.

recommendation.title: Accept after green checks
recommendation.body: Approve the runtime tradeoffs, retain the parity and performance coverage, and merge once every required exact-head check passes.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses embedded-runner scheduling and workspace bootstrap behavior previously shaped by this owner.
